The conjugate whose survival curves lay on top of each other is the warning this class has to answer. The checkpoint result that looks positive is a secondary analysis confined to the patients with evaluable tissue scoring PD-L1-positive. It is not significant.
questions.next: If a conjugate beats chemotherapy after endocrine treatment has failed, does it belong ahead of the first chemotherapy line?

questions.ask: Which endocrine agent should follow an aromatase inhibitor, and does that answer still hold?
questions.rationale: When an aromatase inhibitor fails, the receptor may still be the target. Two strategies were available. Degrade the receptor with fulvestrant, or switch to a steroidal inactivator that binds the enzyme differently. The choice was argued from mechanism for a decade before it was tested.
questions.experiment: Randomisation of fulvestrant against exemestane after progression on a non-steroidal aromatase inhibitor, and separately of fulvestrant with and without added anastrozole against exemestane alone. Later, randomisation of a CDK4/6 inhibitor added to fulvestrant in the same position, and of a degrader combined with everolimus.
questions.finding: Fulvestrant and exemestane were equivalent at the fulvestrant dose those trials used, and adding an aromatase inhibitor to fulvestrant added nothing. What changed the position was not the endocrine agent but what was added to it.
questions.limitation: The two agent comparisons used a fulvestrant dose later shown to be lower than the one now given, so an equivalence result cannot be carried forward unaltered. All of them enrolled patients who had never received a CDK4/6 inhibitor, which is no longer the population in this position.
questions.next: If the endocrine partner is interchangeable and the added agent is what matters, does the choice of partner come down to the alteration found at progression?

stories.title: Molecular exceptions to the endocrine sequence
stories.premise: Almost everything in this cell moves along one path: endocrine therapy with CDK4/6 inhibition, then whatever endocrine option the resistance mechanism still allows, then conjugates and chemotherapy. A small number of these tumours carry an alteration that puts a different drug in front of them. None of those alterations is reported by the assays that assign hormone receptor and HER2 status, and each is found only if someone goes looking for it, in trials that are correspondingly small, biomarker-selected and mostly single-arm.

questions.ask: Does an activating HER2 mutation make a HER2-negative tumour treatable with HER2-directed therapy?
questions.rationale: HER2 status is assigned by protein overexpression and by gene copy number. An activating mutation switches the receptor on without amplifying it. A tumour can therefore signal through HER2 and still score negative on the test that decides who is offered HER2-directed treatment. If the drug answers to the signalling rather than to the copy number, the conventional assay is looking for the wrong thing in these patients.
questions.experiment: Three mutation-selected cohorts gave HER2-directed treatment to disease that was HER2-negative on conventional local testing. One used neratinib with fulvestrant and trastuzumab. One used neratinib with fulvestrant, in cohorts split by previous fulvestrant exposure. One used tucatinib with trastuzumab, with fulvestrant added for the hormone receptor-positive patients. Selection was on the mutation in every case, never on amplification and never on protein expression.
questions.finding: Responses occur in all three. Some of them last. They appear across several different mutations of the receptor, in the kinase domain and in the extracellular domain, and in lobular as well as ductal disease. Selecting on the mutation identifies a treatable population that the amplification assay does not see.
questions.limitation: Every cohort here is single-arm apart from one small randomised substudy inside a basket trial. That substudy set the triplet against fulvestrant-based arms rather than against the chemotherapy these patients would otherwise be offered. The tucatinib cohort is one arm of a solid-tumour basket and reports its intervals at a lower confidence level than the rest of the registry uses. Its response rate therefore does not sit beside the others as a like comparison. Mutations are pooled for the reported result in each trial. One trial did report a class of kinase-domain substitutions that looked worse than the other mutations it enrolled, in an exploratory analysis far too small to act on.
questions.next: Is the mutant receptor an independent driver, or is it an escape route out of oestrogen dependence that hands the tumour back to the endocrine agent once the receptor is blocked?

questions.ask: Does blocking a mutant HER2 restore endocrine sensitivity, or does it work without the endocrine partner?
questions.rationale: HER2 mutations are enriched at relapse on endocrine treatment and in lobular disease. That pattern reads as a route out of oestrogen dependence rather than as a driver that arrived on its own. If it is a route out, blocking the receptor should return the tumour to the endocrine agent that had stopped working. The two drugs would then not be separable.
questions.experiment: One basket study randomised patients carrying a HER2 mutation between fulvestrant alone, fulvestrant with trastuzumab, and the triplet that adds neratinib, with crossover permitted at progression. Another asked the same question by exposure history instead of by randomisation, treating a fulvestrant-pretreated cohort separately from a fulvestrant-naive one. The tucatinib basket cohort gave fulvestrant to its hormone receptor-positive patients and withheld it from the rest.
questions.finding: Neither fulvestrant alone nor fulvestrant with trastuzumab produced a response. Patients who crossed over to the triplet did respond. Clinical benefit appeared in the fulvestrant-pretreated cohort as well as in the fulvestrant-naive one. Previous failure of fulvestrant therefore does not exclude benefit from a combination that contains it.
questions.limitation: The randomised substudy shows that the fulvestrant-based control arms were inert in this population. It cannot measure what neratinib adds, because no arm gave neratinib without fulvestrant. Neratinib alone was given only in an oestrogen receptor-negative cohort, which is a different population and the smallest of the three cohorts in that trial. The two oestrogen receptor-positive cohorts were never randomised against each other and differ in treatment history in every other respect as well. The tucatinib cohort is the one study that gave the endocrine partner to some patients and not to others. It reports response in each group, but receptor status and fulvestrant change together, and the group without fulvestrant is a handful of patients. The only within-trial comparison on offer therefore cannot be read as a test of the endocrine partner.
questions.next: The shape here is general. A genomic test nominates a target. A drug is given. The response rate is read against nothing. Does that reasoning hold where the target is a DNA repair gene and a licensed drug class already exists for one version of the defect?

questions.ask: Does PARP sensitivity extend beyond a germline BRCA mutation?
questions.rationale: The licence for PARP inhibition is written around germline BRCA1 and BRCA2. The mechanism it exploits is a failure of homologous recombination. BRCA is not the only gene whose loss produces that failure. A somatic mutation disables the protein as completely as an inherited one does. If the repair defect is what matters, germline status is a fact about the patient rather than about the tumour.
questions.experiment: Two single-arm trials went outside germline BRCA. One gave olaparib to a germline cohort of repair-gene carriers and to a somatic cohort. The other gave talazoparib to patients wild-type for BRCA1 and BRCA2 whose tumours carried a mutation in a different homologous recombination gene. Standing behind both are the randomised trials that established the class, which set a PARP inhibitor against single-agent chemotherapy of the physician's choice in germline carriers.
questions.finding: Activity did not spread evenly across the genes. It concentrated in germline PALB2 and in somatic BRCA, where the response looked like what germline carriers get from the same drugs in the randomised trials. The remaining repair genes contributed very little. A homologous recombination gene list is therefore not one biomarker. It is several biomarkers that do not behave alike.
questions.limitation: Both trials are single-arm. Both report gene by gene from cohorts of a few patients each. A gene that looks inert here is therefore as uncertain as a gene that looks active. The olaparib trial's registry row carries a BRCA subtype tag although most of its patients had hormone receptor-positive, HER2-negative disease. The row reads as a germline BRCA result when it is not one. The repair deficiency scores that tracked response in the talazoparib study were measured in tumours already chosen for carrying one of these mutations. That correlation cannot show that a score would have selected anyone on its own. Neither trial randomised against the chemotherapy the germline trials used as their comparator. What the drug is worth against that alternative outside BRCA is unmeasured.
questions.next: A marker confirmed only inside a population already selected on it is not yet doing the selecting. The next exception is not a mutation at all. It is a receptor present in most of these tumours that the field has spent its effort trying to block. Does its pharmacology run the other way here?

questions.ask: Can activating the androgen receptor, rather than blocking it, control oestrogen receptor-positive disease?
questions.rationale: The androgen receptor is present in most oestrogen receptor-positive tumours. There it competes with oestrogen-driven transcription rather than supporting it, which makes it a brake and not a driver. The move that follows is agonism. That is the opposite pharmacology to the one tested in receptor-negative disease, where the androgen receptor is what remains once oestrogen signalling has gone.
questions.experiment: A randomised phase II compared one dose of a selective androgen receptor modulator against another, with no standard-therapy arm, in previously treated oestrogen receptor-positive, HER2-negative disease. Its endpoint was clinical benefit at a fixed time point, read in tumours centrally confirmed as androgen receptor-positive. Set beside it for contrast only, two studies of androgen receptor antagonism in receptor-negative disease: bicalutamide in a single arm, and enzalutamide with or without PI3K inhibition.
questions.finding: Agonism produced clinical benefit in a pretreated population, with no advantage to the higher dose over the lower. Antagonism produced benefit in a minority of receptor-negative tumours. Each pharmacology shows activity in the population where the receptor's role runs the way the drug pushes it. The enzalutamide study adds the warning that goes with all of this. Androgen receptor staining alone did not identify which tumours were androgen receptor-dependent, and on an exploratory analysis the luminal androgen receptor transcriptional subtype separated responders from non-responders better than the stain did.
questions.limitation: The randomisation was between one dose of the agonist and another. There is no control arm to read the clinical benefit rate against. Nothing in the trial says whether another endocrine agent would have done as much in the same patients. Central confirmation of androgen receptor positivity defined the population the endpoint describes but was not required for entry. A substantial part of those randomised therefore falls outside the population the result is about. Positivity is in any case a nuclear staining cut-off set by protocol rather than a biological boundary. The antagonist trials state the cut-off they used. The agonist trial's record does not state its own, so the two thresholds cannot be checked against each other. The antagonist trials are here for contrast alone. Their populations are receptor-negative, one is single-arm, and the other randomised its combination against the antagonist alone but reports no result for that alone arm. Nothing on this page compares agonism with antagonism in the same tumour.
questions.next: A population defined by a threshold applied after entry is a hypothesis rather than a rule. What happens when the threshold is the whole message of the trial, a count of mutations that decides who is offered checkpoint blockade?

questions.ask: Can tumour mutational burden select hormone receptor-positive disease for checkpoint blockade?
questions.rationale: This is the least immunogenic of the subtypes. Checkpoint blockade has found no place in it. A small fraction of these tumours are nonetheless hypermutated, often after long endocrine exposure or on a mismatch repair defect. If immune benefit follows neoantigen load rather than receptor status, those tumours should behave like hypermutated cancers elsewhere.
questions.experiment: A single-arm trial gave nivolumab with low-dose ipilimumab to HER2-negative disease entered on a tumour mutational burden above a fixed threshold, with a prespecified correlative analysis at a higher threshold. Beside it sit two studies that did not select on burden at all. A randomised trial added pembrolizumab to a TROP2 conjugate in this subtype without selecting on PD-L1. A rare-histology cohort of a basket study gave the same dual blockade on metaplastic histology alone.
questions.finding: Responses occurred in hypermutated disease. The patients above the higher burden threshold responded more often than those below it. In the randomised setting the checkpoint inhibitor added nothing to the conjugate on the primary endpoint. Its PD-L1-defined subgroup gave a direction rather than a result. The rare-histology cohort cuts the other way. Its few responses were durable. They arose in tumours with low burden, low PD-L1 and no tumour-infiltrating lymphocytes, which is the opposite of what the burden argument would predict.
questions.limitation: The burden-selected trial entered patients on burden within HER2-negative disease, and most of its patients were hormone receptor-positive. The registry tags it across both subtypes for that reason. Its comparison by receptor status was exploratory, so no hormone receptor-positive result can be read out of it. The threshold analysis carrying the selection message rests on a handful of patients and was prespecified as a correlative outcome rather than randomised. It nominates a cut-off and does not validate one. The PD-L1 subgroup in the conjugate trial is a secondary analysis confined to the patients with evaluable tissue, and it was not significant. The rare-histology cohort is one arm of a basket study whose report describes most of its tumours as triple-negative, so it cannot be placed in this subtype at all. Burden is also a property of the panel that counts it. A threshold expressed per megabase of sequence travels between assays less well than it reads.
questions.next: Every exception in this story depends on a test the receptor workup does not perform. Most of these alterations are acquired under treatment rather than present at diagnosis. Which sample is that test supposed to be run on?

questions.ask: Can these alterations be found in the clinic without a fresh biopsy at every progression?
questions.rationale: Each exception here is rare. Most of the alterations arise under treatment. The archival block from the original operation is therefore the wrong sample to interrogate. None of them is reported by the immunohistochemistry that assigns receptor status. The practical limit on all of this is the test rather than the drug.
questions.experiment: A platform trial registered patients on circulating tumour DNA, checked digital PCR against targeted sequencing and both against tissue sequencing, then routed patients into treatment cohorts by the mutation found. One of those cohorts matched a HER2 mutation to neratinib, which is the population the mutation-selected trials above recruited from tissue. Three of those trials carried a plasma measurement of their own alongside the tissue that decided eligibility: acquired HER2 and PIK3CA alterations at progression on the neratinib triplet, repair deficiency scores in plasma as well as in tumour on talazoparib, and serial tumour fraction during treatment in the burden-selected study.
questions.finding: Plasma agreed closely with tissue where the biopsy was contemporaneous. Routing on the plasma result produced responses in the matched cohorts, at rates that differed between cohorts rather than describing the strategy as a whole. The plasma measurements carried alongside the mutation-selected trials tracked what happened on treatment, with a fall or no change in tumour fraction marking benefit. Plasma is workable as the sample that nominates these patients.
questions.limitation: Agreement with tissue was measured where the biopsy was contemporaneous, which is the favourable case. Sensitivity falls when the tissue is older. Older tissue is the situation the plasma test exists to solve. The cohorts were single-arm. A matched response rate says who to treat next, not whether the match beat the alternative. Plasma reports what a tumour sheds. A negative result in low-shedding or bone-only disease is not evidence that the alteration is absent. None of the mutation-selected trials in this story required the alteration to be found in plasma. The eligibility their results describe is a tissue result.
questions.next: A patient can carry more than one of these alterations. Each trial that nominated one made no provision for the others. Which target is acted on first when two are found, and does the order change what the second one is worth?

stories.title: Antibody-drug conjugates after endocrine therapy
stories.premise: When endocrine therapy and its combinations are exhausted, what remains is cytotoxic. Antibody-drug conjugates changed the address of the payload rather than its class, which turns the argument here into a question about what a better address is worth and about whether the antigen that supplies it selects anyone. Underneath every question in this position sits a measurement problem, because the antigens these drugs are named for are scored by assays that were built to answer a different question.

chapters.title: Expression and alteration-defined treatment across subtypes

Conjugates and chemotherapy in later lines

questions.ask: Once endocrine therapy is exhausted, does an antibody-drug conjugate beat the single-agent chemotherapy a clinic would otherwise give?
questions.rationale: The payload inside these conjugates is an ordinary cytotoxic. What the antibody changes is where that payload is delivered, not what it does to a dividing cell. The question was therefore whether a better address buys enough tumour exposure to beat giving the same class of drug systemically and accepting the toxicity that follows.
questions.experiment: Three randomised phase III trials gave a conjugate against physician's choice of single-agent chemotherapy in disease that was hormone receptor-positive and out of endocrine options. They do not all address the same antigen. They also set different requirements for how much chemotherapy a patient had to have had before entry. The control arm in each was drawn from the same short menu of single agents. That menu had been assembled by earlier trials that set those agents against physician's choice and against one another.
questions.finding: Each conjugate lengthened the time to progression against physician's choice chemotherapy. Overall survival did not follow in every case. In the trial that made progression-free survival and overall survival both primary, progression-free survival moved against chemotherapy. Overall survival did not.
questions.limitation: Physician's choice is a composite control rather than a drug. The trials that assembled that menu did not find its members interchangeable in the way the phrase implies. One of them showed a single agent lengthening overall survival against physician's choice in heavily pretreated disease. Another set one menu agent against another and separated them on neither co-primary endpoint. So the comparator is an average of agents whose relative merit was never settled, rather than the drug a particular clinician would have chosen for a particular patient. The three conjugate trials also demanded different amounts of prior chemotherapy before entry. They cannot be stacked into a sequence or read as a ranking. The dual-primary trial is the standing warning here, because it shows that a progression-free survival gain against chemotherapy in this setting does not convert into a survival gain on its own.
questions.next: If the payload does the killing, does the antigen the antibody binds select anyone, or does it only have to be present?

questions.ask: Does the amount of antigen on the tumour select who benefits, or does the antigen only have to be present?
questions.rationale: A conjugate is named for its target. The natural expectation is therefore that more target means more benefit, and that below some level the drug stops working. HER2-low was written as an eligibility category for a trial rather than as a description of a biological class. TROP2 is expressed across almost all of this disease, which makes it a poor candidate for grading anyone.
questions.experiment: The HER2-directed conjugate was tested first in disease scored at the bottom of the conventional HER2 scale. It was then tested in disease scored below even that, including tumours read as negative with only faint membrane staining. Separately, a single-arm study gave the same drug in cohorts spanning the whole expression range, from overexpressing down to no detectable staining. The TROP2 trials did not select on expression at all. One of them measured TROP2 by immunohistochemistry, by immunofluorescence and in plasma, testing each measure against outcome.
questions.finding: In the group scored below the threshold that defined the conjugate's own registration trial, the result was consistent with the group in which that trial's primary comparison was made. Response falls as staining falls and does not disappear where staining is absent. The TROP2 results held across expression subgroups rather than concentrating in the high ones. Where TROP2 was measured by immunohistochemistry, by immunofluorescence and in plasma in one trial, no measure tracked outcome.
questions.limitation: HER2-low and ultralow are scoring conventions on an immunohistochemistry assay designed to find amplification. They are read at the bottom of that assay's range, where agreement between pathologists is at its worst. The category is a property of the assay before it is a property of the tumour. The cohort study spanning the expression range is single-arm. A lower response in a lower-expression cohort therefore carries no chemotherapy comparison inside that cohort and cannot say whether the advantage over chemotherapy differs by expression. The ultralow group in the trial that extended the threshold was exploratory. It sat alongside a primary analysis in the scored-low population rather than testing the threshold itself. No trial has yet randomised anyone on the score.
questions.next: If expression does not select the patient, is the address itself interchangeable, and does redirecting the payload to a different antigen still work after a conjugate has already failed?

questions.ask: Does a second antibody-drug conjugate work after a first one has failed?
questions.rationale: The conjugates used here share a payload mechanism while differing in the antibody. If resistance is to the payload, changing the antibody buys nothing. If it is to the target, to its internalisation or to trafficking inside the cell, a different address might still work. Patients now arrive in later lines having already had a conjugate. The question has stopped being theoretical.
questions.experiment: A HER3-directed conjugate was given as a single arm after progression on CDK4/6 inhibition and a line of chemotherapy. Paired baseline and on-treatment biopsies were taken, to see how far the drug distributed inside the tumour and what the tumour did in response. A prospective study is now assigning a second conjugate after a first, in separate cohorts defined by which conjugate came before.
questions.finding: Redirecting the payload to a third antigen met its response endpoint in a population already treated with CDK4/6 inhibition and chemotherapy. The on-treatment tissue work associated efficacy with how far the conjugate distributed within the tumour and with an interferon response. At baseline the associations ran to where the receptor sat in the tissue and to the absence of an ESR1 mutation, with receptor level itself tracking only the progression endpoint.
questions.limitation: The HER3 study is single-arm. Its response rate has nothing to be read against and cannot rank HER3 delivery against another conjugate or against chemotherapy. That response is reported with a narrower confidence interval than the randomised trials beside it use, which is what a single-arm design of this kind specifies and not a sign of greater precision. The on-treatment biopsies come only from patients who stayed on the drug long enough to be rebiopsied. That is selection on the very outcome the biomarkers are being asked to explain. The authors state that every association is pending validation. The prospective sequencing study is still running. Its cohorts are non-comparative by design. It will report activity after a conjugate rather than the value of a sequence.
questions.next: If the limit is the payload rather than the address, does adding checkpoint blockade to the conjugate make it work harder?

questions.ask: Does adding checkpoint blockade to a TROP2 conjugate improve on the conjugate alone?
questions.rationale: A topoisomerase payload kills in a way that releases tumour antigen and can draw immune cells into the tumour, which is the standard argument for putting a conjugate next to a checkpoint inhibitor. Hormone receptor-positive disease is the least immunogenic of the common subtypes. If a conjugate is what makes a tumour visible to the immune system, this is where an added effect should be easiest to attribute to the conjugate rather than to the tumour's own starting immunogenicity.
questions.experiment: A randomised phase II trial gave a TROP2 conjugate with or without a checkpoint inhibitor, in disease pretreated with endocrine therapy and at most one chemotherapy regimen. Progression-free survival was the primary endpoint. The PD-L1-positive population was a key secondary one. A phase III trial is now testing the same addition with a different TROP2 conjugate, ahead of any chemotherapy, against physician's choice chemotherapy. Elsewhere in this subtype, checkpoint blockade has been given either in single-arm combinations, where the partner drug cannot be separated from the checkpoint inhibitor, or in populations selected for a high mutational burden.
questions.finding: Adding the checkpoint inhibitor did not improve progression-free survival over the conjugate alone in the population unselected for PD-L1. The PD-L1-positive subgroup pointed in the favourable direction without reaching significance. Elsewhere in this subtype, checkpoint blockade has produced responses only where the population was selected for a mutational phenotype.
questions.limitation: The PD-L1 result is a key secondary analysis, confined to the patients who had evaluable tissue and scored positive on it. It did not reach significance. Its own authors describe it as a trend for larger randomised trials to test rather than as a result. Eligibility also allowed entry with no chemotherapy at all for metastatic disease, and much of the enrolled population came in on that basis. The trial therefore sits earlier in the course than the line at which this conjugate is registered in this subtype. A single line label is covering a mixed population. The single-arm combination that sits beside it cannot establish what its checkpoint inhibitor added, as its authors say themselves, so it supplies no counterweight in either direction. The mutational-burden study selected on a threshold that its own correlative subgroup was too small to fix. It says that selection matters without saying where the line falls. The randomised comparison here is phase II and was not sized to exclude the size of effect a phase III would chase. The phase III now putting the same addition ahead of chemotherapy is the trial that will settle it.
questions.next: If neither a partner drug nor a measured biomarker improves on the conjugate, does the remaining lever become where in the sequence the conjugate is given?

questions.ask: Should a conjugate replace the first chemotherapy rather than follow it?
questions.rationale: Every trial that established these drugs enrolled after chemotherapy had already been given. What they measured is the value of a conjugate at that point in the course. Moving it forward means giving a drug with its own distinctive toxicity to people who might have done well for a long time on one gentle cytotoxic. It also means giving it to people who might not have needed cytotoxic treatment at all yet.
questions.experiment: One phase III trial moved the HER2-directed conjugate ahead of any chemotherapy for metastatic disease in endocrine-pretreated patients, against physician's choice chemotherapy. Two TROP2 trials are doing the same in the first chemotherapy slot and have not reported. From the opposite direction, a randomised trial in aggressive disease compared endocrine therapy with a CDK4/6 inhibitor against combination chemotherapy, asking whether cytotoxic treatment was needed at that point at all.
questions.finding: The conjugate given before any chemotherapy lengthened time to progression against physician's choice chemotherapy, with overall survival immature at that analysis. Endocrine therapy with a CDK4/6 inhibitor outlasted combination chemotherapy in aggressive disease that would once have gone straight to cytotoxic treatment. Both results push conventional single-agent chemotherapy out of the slot it used to hold, from opposite directions.
questions.limitation: The control arm in the earlier-line conjugate trial is the same physician's-choice menu. Its overall survival was immature at the primary analysis. A longer time to first progression is currently the whole of the case for moving the drug forward. The aggressive-disease trial is phase II and premenopausal. It enrolled on a clinical judgement of aggressiveness rather than on a stated threshold. It therefore does not define who can safely be kept off chemotherapy. Most of all, no trial here randomised the order of the same drugs. The design that would answer that randomises the position and then measures progression on the line after next. That is how the first-line CDK4/6 question was settled. It is not how any conjugate in this position has been studied.
questions.next: Does giving the conjugate earlier lengthen the whole sequence or only its first segment, and will any conjugate trial measure the second progression rather than the first?

questions.ask: Once chemotherapy is reached, does the choice of agent matter?
questions.rationale: Two newer taxane formulations and an epothilone were developed to improve on weekly paclitaxel. The argument was that a different delivery vehicle, or a different tubulin-binding site, would raise response or lower toxicity. Each had promising single-arm data before the comparison was run.
questions.experiment: Three-arm randomisation of weekly nab-paclitaxel and weekly ixabepilone against weekly paclitaxel, each with bevacizumab, in chemotherapy-naive advanced disease.
questions.finding: Neither experimental agent improved progression-free survival and one was clearly worse. The oldest and cheapest arm was the best of the three.
questions.limitation: The comparison was made in the first-line position with a bevacizumab backbone, and the chapter that carries it is about later lines where the alternatives are conjugates rather than single agents. A negative result against paclitaxel does not establish how any of these agents performs after a conjugate has failed.
questions.next: If single-agent chemotherapy has a settled answer, is the remaining question only when to stop reaching for a conjugate and use it?

stories.title: Layering HER2 blockade and choosing what follows it
stories.premise: Almost everything that works at this position works through one receptor, by blocking it, by using it as an address for a cytotoxic, or by leaning on what its antibody does to the immune system. The questions here are therefore not whether to target HER2, but how many ways to block it, what to attach to it, and whether the target is still there to aim at. The answers arrived as a chain of trials, each tested against the standard of its own year rather than against the order a clinic now uses.

chapters.title: When the target changes, and when to stop blocking it
Metastatic therapy from first line onwards

questions.ask: Does blocking HER2 at more than one site do more than blocking it at one?
questions.rationale: HER2 has no ligand of its own. It signals by pairing. Its most active partner is HER3, which is ligand-driven. Trastuzumab binds the membrane-proximal domain and leaves the dimerisation arm exposed. Ligand-driven pairing therefore continues underneath it. A second antibody aimed at that arm, or a small molecule that shuts the kinase down from inside the cell, should close an escape the first antibody never covered.
questions.experiment: A sequence of first-line randomised trials, each adding one more layer to the layer below. Trastuzumab added to chemotherapy, in a large trial and again in a small one. Then pertuzumab added to trastuzumab and a taxane. Then a HER2 kinase inhibitor added to trastuzumab and a taxane in one trial, and added to trastuzumab with pertuzumab as maintenance in another. A large single-arm study ran alongside them, giving the same antibody pair with whichever taxane the investigator chose.
questions.finding: Adding the first antibody to chemotherapy delayed progression and lengthened overall survival, against the same chemotherapy given alone. Adding the second antibody did both again, against a single antibody given with the same taxane. Adding a kinase inhibitor delayed progression in both trials that tried it, each against the regimen it was added to. The kinase inhibitor added to the taxane doublet has since reported an overall survival advantage over that doublet. The kinase inhibitor added to the antibody pair as maintenance has not reported overall survival at all. The endpoint is not constant along the chain. The earliest trials measured time to progression or response rate rather than progression-free survival, so a longer interval is not the same measurement at both ends of it. The single-arm study reported tolerability for the antibody pair with each of the three taxanes, and had no comparator to rank them.
questions.limitation: These trials were run against the standard of their own year, so the additions are not stacked on one backbone. The first layer rests on one large trial with a time-to-progression endpoint and one small trial whose primary endpoint was response rate, so the two are not the same grade of evidence. CLEOPATRA's control arm had none of the drugs that now follow first-line progression. The survival difference it measured therefore belongs to a sequence rather than to pertuzumab alone. PHILA's control arm was trastuzumab and docetaxel without pertuzumab, so it says what a kinase inhibitor adds to a doublet rather than what it adds to the triplet a clinic now starts with. It also enrolled in one country. HER2CLIMB-05 randomised only patients who had not progressed during induction, so its population is selected for disease the backbone already controls. PERUSE had safety as its primary endpoint and no comparator at all, so its efficacy figures describe a cohort rather than test anything.
questions.next: If a third layer of HER2 blockade beats two, what is the free taxane still doing in the regimen?

questions.ask: Does the cytotoxic have to be given as free chemotherapy, or can it travel on the antibody?
questions.rationale: A conjugate uses the antibody as a delivery vehicle. The cytotoxic should concentrate where the antigen is displayed and spare tissue that does not display it. If that holds at the front of the disease course, the free taxane is doing nothing the conjugate does not do better. The stronger version of the idea drops the cytotoxic altogether, on the argument that a HER2-dependent tumour can be held by blockade alone.
questions.experiment: Two first-line randomised trials substituted a conjugate for the taxane. One compared trastuzumab emtansine, alone and with pertuzumab, against trastuzumab plus a taxane. The other compared trastuzumab deruxtecan plus pertuzumab against the taxane, trastuzumab and pertuzumab triplet, and carried a third arm of the conjugate alone. An early-phase programme is giving the newer conjugate alone and in combinations in the same line. The chemotherapy-free version of the question was asked twice and separately. A single-arm study gave lapatinib with trastuzumab across two cohorts defined by prior treatment. A randomised trial gave lapatinib with or without trastuzumab in disease progressing on trastuzumab.
questions.finding: The first-generation conjugate was noninferior to the taxane backbone and was not superior to it, with or without the second antibody. The newer conjugate with the second antibody delayed progression against the triplet. Chemotherapy-free dual blockade produced responses in a cohort untreated for metastatic disease and in a pretreated cohort, more often in the untreated one. Where blockade without chemotherapy was randomised against less blockade without chemotherapy, the pair delayed progression and lengthened overall survival against the single agent.
questions.limitation: Noninferiority is a claim about a prespecified margin rather than a demonstration that two regimens are the same. MARIANNE's primary publication reported no overall survival at all. DESTINY-Breast09's third arm, the conjugate without pertuzumab, was still blinded at the interim analysis, so nothing yet separates what the conjugate contributes from what the second antibody contributes. Its overall survival is not reported either. DESTINY-Breast07 has no publication on the record, so it names a programme rather than a result. TBCRC 003 is single-arm and its two cohorts were defined by prior treatment, so the gap between their response rates is a difference between populations rather than a comparison. A chemotherapy-free response rate from that era cannot stand as a comparator for a modern chemotherapy-containing regimen. EGF104900 did drop the cytotoxic, but it set its pair against a single kinase inhibitor rather than against any chemotherapy-containing regimen. It therefore says nothing about how chemotherapy-free blockade stands against the triplet a clinic starts with.
questions.next: If the cytotoxic can be carried on the antibody or left out at the start, is the receptor still worth blocking once the disease has progressed on drugs aimed at it?

questions.ask: Is HER2 still worth blocking once the disease has progressed on HER2 blockade?
questions.rationale: Progression on trastuzumab admits two readings. Either the tumour has stopped depending on HER2, in which case the target should be abandoned. Or it has escaped one way of blocking a receptor it still needs, in which case the target should be attacked differently. The two readings imply opposite prescriptions. Only a trial that holds the chemotherapy fixed and varies the blockade can tell them apart.
questions.experiment: Randomised trials that held the chemotherapy fixed and varied only the HER2 blockade after progression on trastuzumab. Capecitabine with continued trastuzumab against capecitabine alone. Capecitabine with lapatinib against capecitabine alone. Lapatinib with or without trastuzumab in disease already progressing on trastuzumab, with no chemotherapy in either arm. Further down the course, and holding nothing fixed, a conjugate against whatever the physician would otherwise have chosen.
questions.finding: Both capecitabine trials delayed progression against capecitabine given alone, one by continuing the antibody through progression and one by adding a kinase inhibitor. Blocking the receptor at two sites delayed progression and lengthened overall survival against blocking it at one, in disease already progressing on one of them. Later in the course the conjugate delayed progression against whatever else would have been given. The target survives progression on the drugs aimed at it.
questions.limitation: These are separate trials with separate control arms. Two of those arms are weak by design. EGF104900 compared lapatinib plus trastuzumab against lapatinib alone, which is not a regimen a clinic would choose for anyone. TH3RESA's comparator was physician's choice in heavily pretreated disease, which is a floor rather than a standard, and it varied the chemotherapy as well as the blockade. GBG 26 randomised a small population against a time-to-progression endpoint. Its overall survival difference was not significant, so it shows that continuing the antibody delays progression rather than that it extends life. EGF100151 stopped at an interim analysis for superiority in time to progression, and its final overall survival did not separate. None of these trials required a repeat biopsy at progression, so the receptor's persistence is inferred from the fact that drugs against it still work rather than measured.
questions.next: If the receptor stays worth blocking through successive lines, in what order should the drugs aimed at it be given?

questions.ask: In what order should the later-line HER2 drugs be given?
questions.rationale: After the first-line triplet the choices are a conjugate, a kinase inhibitor with an oral cytotoxic, or another antibody. Each was developed against whatever was standard when it entered trial. So the sequence a clinic uses was assembled from a chain of comparisons rather than chosen in any one of them.
questions.experiment: A conjugate against a kinase inhibitor with capecitabine, after trastuzumab and a taxane. A newer conjugate against that conjugate in the same line. The newer conjugate against physician's choice in disease that had already progressed on the older one. A kinase inhibitor added to the older conjugate. One kinase inhibitor against another with the same oral partner, early in the sequence and again late. A kinase inhibitor added to trastuzumab and capecitabine in heavily pretreated disease.
questions.finding: Every one of these comparisons favoured the newer agent, or the more heavily blocked arm, on its own progression endpoint. Overall survival did not follow everywhere. It separated for the conjugate against the kinase inhibitor doublet, for the newer conjugate against the older one, and for the kinase inhibitor added to trastuzumab and capecitabine. It did not separate for one kinase inhibitor against another with the same oral partner in the latest line. It ran the wrong way at the interim analysis for the kinase inhibitor added to the older conjugate. The single head-to-head of the two conjugates was decisive enough to move the newer one into second line. The order a clinic now uses is a reading across that chain rather than the result of any trial in it.
questions.limitation: No trial randomised the order. The controls are era-specific, and EMILIA's kinase inhibitor doublet is no longer what a clinic would put in a control arm. Physician's choice inside a conjugate trial is not the set of options a clinic would now reach for, so the separation measured against it overstates what the drug adds today. DESTINY-Breast02's second-line label is a floor rather than a description, because entry required only progression on trastuzumab emtansine and capped nothing before that. HER2CLIMB-02 improved progression-free survival against the conjugate alone while its interim overall survival ran the other way, which is not a shape a sequencing decision can be built on. PHOEBE's result is a prespecified interim analysis and its comparator has since been displaced. HER2CLIMB and NALA both admitted patients with brain metastases, so part of what they measured belongs to the central nervous system question rather than to this one.
questions.next: If no trial randomised the order, can the next drug be chosen by measuring the target rather than by counting previous lines?

questions.ask: Can the next drug be chosen by measuring the target rather than by counting previous lines?
questions.rationale: A patient's HER2 status is usually assigned once, on the primary tumour, by an immunohistochemistry cut-off chosen to select for trastuzumab. Metastatic deposits are not obliged to match the primary, and they are not obliged to match each other. If the antigen can be measured in the disease actually being treated, the choice of the next drug could rest on the target rather than on the treatment history.
questions.experiment: Three ways of measuring rather than counting. Imaging the antigen with a labelled antibody before giving a conjugate, read alongside an early metabolic scan. An early metabolic response read embedded in the chemotherapy-free dual blockade study. A conjugate given to prespecified cohorts defined by immunohistochemistry score, from overexpressing through low down to no detectable staining. Set against those, the registration study that gave a newer conjugate to disease that had already failed an older conjugate aimed at the same antigen.
questions.finding: Antigen imaging found patients whose lesions took up no tracer, and found uneven uptake within single patients. Its predictive values against radiological response improved when the early metabolic scan was read with it. In the chemotherapy-free study, absence of an early metabolic response predicted failure to respond by imaging criteria, and did so in both cohorts. The conjugate produced responses in every staining cohort, most often in the overexpressing one and not rarely in the cohort scored as non-expressing. Failure of one conjugate aimed at HER2 did not predict failure of the next.
questions.limitation: These are measurement studies rather than allocation trials. A predictive value is computed in one cohort all treated the same way, against a radiological definition of response. It describes how a scan tracks an outcome rather than showing that acting on the scan changes one. Nobody has randomised patients to be allocated by imaging. DAISY's cohorts were cut from a central immunohistochemistry score, so the boundary between them is an assay convention rather than a biological class. Each cohort was single-arm, so activity in the non-expressing cohort may be reporting the floor of that assay rather than activity without the target. The metabolic read in TBCRC 003 sat inside a single-arm study, which gives its predictive claim the same shape. DESTINY-Breast01 had no control arm, so it cannot say whether the second conjugate worked because the antigen persisted or because its payload differs.
questions.next: If measuring the target still leaves patients whose disease carries it and progresses anyway, can a mechanism other than HER2 blockade be added to extend what HER2 blockade can do?

questions.ask: Can a mechanism other than HER2 blockade be added to extend what HER2 blockade can do?
questions.rationale: Part of trastuzumab's effect is immune. It engages Fc receptors on effector cells. The response to it tracks with the lymphocytic infiltrate in the tumour. Two routes follow from that. Re-engineer the Fc so it binds the low-affinity receptor allele better, or take the brake off the effector cells with a checkpoint antibody. A third route has nothing to do with the immune system. HER2 amplification is associated with replication stress, which raised the possibility that a PARP inhibitor would work here without a germline BRCA variant.
questions.experiment: An Fc-engineered anti-HER2 antibody against trastuzumab, each with chemotherapy, randomised in pretreated disease. Pembrolizumab added to trastuzumab in a single-arm study, with PD-L1 scored centrally on a metastatic biopsy and with parallel PD-L1-positive and PD-L1-negative cohorts. Atezolizumab or placebo added to trastuzumab emtansine, randomised. Niraparib added to trastuzumab with no germline selection.
questions.finding: The engineered antibody delayed progression against trastuzumab given with the same chemotherapy. Its final overall survival did not favour it. Checkpoint blockade added to trastuzumab produced responses only in PD-L1-positive tumours, and in a minority of those. Added to the conjugate in a randomised design, checkpoint blockade did not meet its primary endpoint. The PARP combination has produced no full report.
questions.limitation: PANACEA is single-arm, so its responses cannot be separated from what trastuzumab alone would have done in a PD-L1-selected group. Its PD-L1 scoring was central and required a metastatic biopsy, which is not how the marker is obtained in clinic. Its headline response applies to the PD-L1-positive cohort of the expansion stage rather than to everyone treated. KATE2 was unmasked early for futility, so follow-up is short on both arms. The PD-L1-positive subgroup its authors argue for is not reported as a subgroup result, so the case for pursuing it rests on an analysis nobody can read. TBCRC 050 sits on the record only as conference material, with nothing stated about enrolment, endpoint or result, so it names a strategy under test rather than a finding. SOPHIA separated on progression-free survival without a survival difference, which leaves the Fc hypothesis neither confirmed nor refuted. Its genotype analysis was exploratory and pointed one way for the low-affinity allele and the other way for the high-affinity one, so it generates the hypothesis it is often read as supporting.
questions.next: Does the immune combination belong earlier in the course, before repeated HER2 blockade has thinned the infiltrate? And is the escape being chased here immune at all, rather than the luminal biology that the hormone receptor-positive half of this disease carries?

stories.title: The luminal half of a HER2-driven cancer
stories.premise: A tumour that is both hormone receptor-positive and HER2-positive runs on two pathways that prop each other up, each rising when the other is suppressed. Nearly every practice-defining HER2 trial enrolled both receptor groups and reported them together, which left what is specific to the triple-positive patient to smaller trials off to one side. The questions here are whether the luminal half of that biology is worth treating in its own right, when in the course to treat it, and in whom.

chapters.title: Metastatic triple-positive disease

questions.ask: Does a tumour that is both hormone receptor-positive and HER2-positive need both pathways blocked?
questions.rationale: The two pathways hold each other up. Blocking HER2 restores oestrogen receptor signalling. Blocking the receptor pushes growth signalling back through HER2. Either drug given alone therefore leaves an escape route open.
questions.experiment: Chemotherapy-free randomisations in this cell built the case in two steps. TAnDEM and EGF30008 added a HER2-directed drug to an aromatase inhibitor. PERTAIN and ALTERNATIVE added a second HER2-directed drug to that pair. EGF30008 enrolled hormone receptor-positive patients regardless of HER2 status and made the HER2-positive group its prespecified primary analysis. ALTERNATIVE asked its question in patients who had already had trastuzumab and endocrine therapy.
questions.finding: Each addition delayed progression against the regimen it was added to. In the trial that enrolled both HER2 groups the gain appeared only where HER2 was amplified. That is an internal control the single-subtype trials do not have.
questions.limitation: Every control arm here is a regimen no clinic would now offer, either endocrine therapy alone or a single antibody with endocrine therapy. ALTERNATIVE enrolled only patients for whom chemotherapy was not intended, which selects on a clinician's judgement rather than on anything measured. Most of TAnDEM's endocrine-only arm crossed to trastuzumab on progression, leaving its survival comparison unable to settle anything. PERTAIN's own overall survival came out no different between its arms. None of these trials set the chemotherapy-free combination against dual blockade with a taxane.
questions.next: If endocrine therapy with HER2 blockade controls this disease at all, can it stand in for chemotherapy rather than be arranged around it?

questions.ask: Can endocrine therapy stand in for chemotherapy alongside HER2-directed treatment?
questions.rationale: First-line treatment pairs HER2 blockade with a taxane, on the record CLEOPATRA built. The taxane is the part the patient pays for. If the tumour depends on oestrogen as much as on HER2, an endocrine agent is the cheaper partner for the antibody.
questions.experiment: SYSUCC-002 randomised untreated metastatic patients to trastuzumab with endocrine therapy or trastuzumab with chemotherapy. It was powered to show that the endocrine partner was not worse than the cytotoxic one by more than a prespecified margin on progression-free survival. PERTAIN puts a version of the same question informally, because induction chemotherapy in it was left to investigator discretion.
questions.finding: The endocrine partner met the noninferiority margin against chemotherapy for time to progression, at lower toxicity than the chemotherapy arm carried. In PERTAIN, among the patients who had no induction chemotherapy at all, adding the second antibody to endocrine therapy separated the arms at least as far as it did in the trial as a whole.
questions.limitation: The SYSUCC-002 control was a single antibody with chemotherapy rather than the dual blockade with a taxane that CLEOPATRA had already made standard. Noninferiority was therefore shown against a comparator its own era had improved on. Its margin was set on progression-free survival. Its overall survival is not yet reported, so what is being traded for the lower toxicity remains unmeasured. The PERTAIN comparison is not randomised at all, because induction was an investigator's decision. Its chemotherapy-free group is a group judged not to need chemotherapy.
questions.next: If the endocrine partner can carry a whole line, can it also carry one after HER2-directed treatment has failed, where chemotherapy is the default?

questions.ask: After HER2-directed regimens have failed, does a CDK4/6 inhibitor with trastuzumab and endocrine therapy beat returning to chemotherapy?
questions.rationale: Cyclin D1 and CDK4/6 sit downstream of both the oestrogen receptor and HER2, which makes them the node where the two pathways converge. Escape from HER2 blockade runs through that node. Blocking it would also put a chemotherapy-free option into a line where chemotherapy is the default.
questions.experiment: monarcHER randomised pretreated triple-positive patients three ways: abemaciclib with trastuzumab and fulvestrant, abemaciclib with trastuzumab, and physician's choice chemotherapy with trastuzumab. The two-drug arm carries the same CDK4/6 inhibitor without the endocrine partner, which is what isolates the endocrine contribution. SOLTI-1303 PATRICIA later ran the same three-drug idea against trastuzumab-based physician's choice in a comparably pretreated population.
questions.finding: Only the arm carrying the endocrine partner improved on chemotherapy for time to progression. The same CDK4/6 inhibitor without it was no better than chemotherapy. Overall survival ran in the same direction on a comparison that carried no alpha of its own.
questions.limitation: This was a screening phase II. Its progression-free survival result was declared against a significance threshold much looser than a phase III would use, which makes it a signal to be confirmed rather than a confirmation. Its chemotherapy control predates DESTINY-Breast03, which moved the conjugate into the line ahead of this one and changed what a patient now arrives here having already had. Entry turned on receptor positivity by immunohistochemistry, with no requirement that the tumour behave as a luminal one.
questions.next: If the endocrine partner is what makes the combination work, does the tumour have to be luminal by more than a receptor stain?

questions.ask: Does the benefit hold only in tumours that are luminal by intrinsic subtype, rather than in every tumour that stains receptor-positive?
questions.rationale: Receptor positivity is a protein stain read against a scoring threshold. Intrinsic subtyping reads the transcriptional programme instead. A substantial share of receptor-positive, HER2-positive tumours classify as HER2-enriched rather than luminal. If the luminal programme is what the endocrine drug and the CDK4/6 inhibitor exploit, then the stain is only a proxy for the thing being selected on.
questions.experiment: SOLTI-1303 PATRICIA ran single-arm cohorts of palbociclib with trastuzumab, split by oestrogen receptor status and given with or without letrozole. On a secondary analysis, luminal tumours ran longer before progressing than non-luminal ones. The trial then closed those cohorts and opened a randomised one restricted to PAM50 luminal disease, comparing palbociclib with trastuzumab and endocrine therapy against trastuzumab-based treatment of physician's choice.
questions.finding: In the subtype-restricted randomised cohort the triplet delayed progression against physician's choice. A tail of patients on the triplet was still free of progression long after almost everyone on physician's choice had progressed.
questions.limitation: The subtype rule was derived in this study's own earlier cohorts and then tested in a cohort built around it. No randomised non-luminal comparison exists to show that the rule excludes anyone correctly. The control arm was trastuzumab-based treatment of the investigator's choosing, which put a conjugate, chemotherapy and endocrine therapy into a single comparator. Patients allocated to that arm could be randomised again on progression, leaving more randomised assignments than distinct participants. The cohort reports no overall survival.
questions.next: If subtype picks out who benefits after HER2-directed lines have failed, does the same selection apply earlier, where a CDK4/6 inhibitor is given to everyone whose disease has responded to induction?

questions.ask: Is the right moment for a CDK4/6 inhibitor the maintenance phase after induction, rather than a later line?
questions.rationale: First-line treatment in this cell ends in a long maintenance phase on HER2-directed and endocrine therapy, with the disease quiet and the residual burden small. Holding proliferation down is exactly what a CDK4/6 inhibitor does. monarcHER and SOLTI-1303 PATRICIA handed the class tumours that had already escaped several HER2-directed lines and had time to find other routes.
questions.experiment: PATINA randomised patients whose disease had not progressed after induction chemotherapy with HER2-directed treatment. One arm added palbociclib to maintenance HER2-directed and endocrine therapy. The other continued that maintenance alone. No subtype or biomarker selection was applied.
questions.finding: Adding the CDK4/6 inhibitor lengthened the maintenance phase against the same maintenance without it, in an unselected receptor-positive population. It also brought the neutropenia the class brings into a phase in which patients feel well.
questions.limitation: Randomisation came after induction, selecting a population whose disease did not progress on chemotherapy with HER2 blockade. The trial says what palbociclib adds to a patient who is already responding, not what it adds to everyone who starts first line. Its overall survival is not yet reported. Its induction belongs to the era CLEOPATRA defined, and DESTINY-Breast09 has since moved first-line treatment to a conjugate with dual blockade. The maintenance phase PATINA improved is therefore not quite the one a clinic will be managing.
questions.next: If first-line induction becomes an antibody-drug conjugate with dual blockade, is there still a maintenance phase to put an endocrine and CDK4/6 backbone into, and would the subtype assay be needed to find the patients for it?

stories.title: Finding something to aim at in a disease defined by absence
stories.premise: Triple-negative is the output of three negative assays, so the name says what the tumour lacks and nothing about what it needs. Every question in this cell is therefore a search for something to aim at. The things that have changed practice here were not lineage targets at all, but a repair defect, an immune infiltrate and a surface antigen, each carrying a measurement problem of its own.

chapters.title: The biomarker triage, and what is left when it finds nothing
Metastatic therapy from first line onwards

questions.ask: Does naming a molecular dependency inside triple-negative disease produce a subset that a drug can be aimed at?
questions.rationale: The definition names no driver, so the search has been for whatever else the tumour depends on. Expression profiling supplied the candidates: epidermal growth factor receptor signalling, death receptor signalling, the androgen receptor, and the PI3K-AKT pathway. Each looked like a receptor-defined subtype waiting for its own drug.
questions.experiment: Each candidate was tested by adding its agent to chemotherapy, or by giving it alone in a population selected for the marker. EGFR antibody blockade went with carboplatin, and a death receptor agonist with a taxane. One androgen receptor antagonist was given alone to tumours staining positive for the receptor. A second antagonist was then randomised with and without a PI3K inhibitor. The AKT axis was carried furthest. Two randomised phase II trials added an AKT inhibitor to paclitaxel in unselected untreated disease. Two phase III trials followed, one restricting entry to tumours carrying a PIK3CA, AKT1 or PTEN alteration, the other enrolling regardless and reading the altered tumours alongside the whole population from testing done after the fact.
questions.finding: Every candidate produced responses in somebody. None produced a group that a controlled comparison could separate from the rest. The AKT axis is the clearest case. Both phase II trials favoured the AKT inhibitor on progression-free survival, and both phase III trials were negative, the one that admitted only pathway-altered tumours and the one that read the altered tumours inside an unselected population. Selection had already failed once inside the phase II work, where the trial that prespecified a PTEN-low population separated nothing in it.
questions.limitation: Most of these designs cannot say what the added agent contributed. The EGFR trial crossed over by protocol, so the same patients supply more than one response group. The death receptor trial set its primary endpoint as the response rate within each arm rather than the difference between arms. The two androgen receptor trials fail in different ways. The bicalutamide trial asked for oestrogen and progesterone receptor negativity and said nothing about HER2, so its enrolled population is wider than the cell it is filed under. The enzalutamide trial reports a clinical benefit rate for the combination and none for the antagonist given alone, and its dose-finding part admitted oestrogen receptor-positive patients. The AKT programme changed the question between phases, and it did so differently for each drug. One phase II trial read progression-free survival against a one-sided threshold, and the phase III trial of that same drug read overall survival as a primary endpoint, so the measurement that justified going forward is not the measurement that refuted it. The phase III trial of the other drug kept progression-free survival but moved to a biomarker-restricted population, so it never tested the population the phase II signal came from.
questions.next: If a receptor or a pathway does not define a treatable subset, does a functional defect in DNA repair do better, and can it be measured in a tumour with no germline mutation?

questions.ask: Does any measure of defective DNA repair select who benefits from platinum, beyond a germline BRCA mutation?
questions.rationale: Triple-negative tumours carry genomic scars that resemble those of BRCA1-mutant cancers. Platinum kills cells that cannot repair a crosslink. If the resemblance is functional rather than cosmetic, an assay of repair ought to find platinum responders among the large majority who carry no germline mutation.
questions.experiment: Single-agent platinum was given in a single-arm trial with a gene expression predictor written in as a coprimary endpoint. Platinum was then randomised against a taxane in unselected advanced disease, with germline BRCA and several other repair-defect markers prespecified as interaction tests. A platinum doublet was randomised against a taxane doublet in untreated disease, gemcitabine sitting in both arms, and tested for non-inferiority before superiority. Two further trials asked the same question of PARP inhibition. One added a PARP inhibitor to platinum and taxane in germline carriers. The other gave a PARP inhibitor alone to tumours wild-type for BRCA1 and BRCA2 that carried a mutation in another repair gene.
questions.finding: Platinum holds its own against a taxane in unselected disease. The single-agent comparison found no difference in response rate between carboplatin and docetaxel, and the doublet comparison favoured the platinum arm on progression-free survival. Germline BRCA status is the one marker that tracks response wherever it was measured, raising the response to carboplatin in the randomised trial and to single-agent platinum in the single-arm one. Nothing else reproduced it. The prespecified expression predictor failed outright, the commercial instability score carried as an interaction test in the randomised trial showed no effect, and the panel of other repair genes gave regressions only in a single gene and only on very few patients.
questions.limitation: The predictive claims rest on subgroups and on single arms rather than on randomised selection. In the platinum monotherapy trial the choice between cisplatin and carboplatin was left to the treating physician, so the two agents are not being compared. Its germline carriers were a subgroup rather than an entry criterion, and there were very few of them. Its prespecified expression predictor was the negative half of a coprimary endpoint, while the genomic instability analyses that did separate responders there were exploratory and did not survive the randomised trial's prespecified test of an instability score. The randomised single-agent comparison read objective response rate as its primary endpoint, so a difference in how long benefit lasted would not have shown in it. Its progression-free and overall survival, read as secondary endpoints, showed no difference between the arms. The doublet comparison enrolled untreated patients at Chinese centres only, so its superiority is not a general statement about platinum against a taxane at any line. The trial that added a PARP inhibitor to platinum and taxane required a germline mutation but allowed any HER2-negative disease, so hormone receptor-positive patients sit inside a result filed here.
questions.next: If the one marker that holds names a minority, does the immune compartment offer a marker for anyone else?

questions.ask: Does the PD-L1 assay identify who gains from a checkpoint inhibitor, whether it is added to first-line chemotherapy or given alone?
questions.rationale: Triple-negative tumours carry more lymphocytic infiltrate and more PD-L1 than the other subtypes do. Only a minority of them carry either. A checkpoint inhibitor can release a response only where one already exists, so each trial carried a companion assay meant to find the tumours where it does.
questions.experiment: Four randomised first-line trials added a checkpoint inhibitor to a chemotherapy backbone and compared it against the same backbone alone. They differ in the checkpoint antibody, in the chemotherapy partner, and in how PD-L1 was stained, scored and thresholded. Two used nab-paclitaxel, one a plain taxane, and one allowed a choice of backbones. A fifth trial gave the checkpoint inhibitor alone against the physician's choice of chemotherapy after prior treatment, with the score as the stratifying question.
questions.finding: Survival benefit is confined to the assay-positive population. The trial that read overall survival by score found it only above the higher cut-off, and it did not reach significance in everyone enrolled. Progression-free survival is less tidy than the selection story suggests, because in the first atezolizumab trial it improved in the whole enrolled population as well as in the assay-positive subgroup. Nothing appeared at all in the trial that paired the same antibody with a plain taxane, at any level of the score. Given alone after prior treatment, a checkpoint inhibitor did not beat chemotherapy at either score threshold tested.
questions.limitation: There is no single PD-L1 test in this set. The trials used different antibodies, scored different compartments, tumour cells against immune cells against a combined count, and set different cut-offs. A patient positive in one trial is not necessarily positive in another. The discordance between the two atezolizumab trials is a comparison across trials rather than a randomised one. Those two differ in the taxane, in the corticosteroid premedication a plain taxane requires, and in the population enrolled, so the failure cannot be assigned to the backbone alone. In the first atezolizumab trial the hierarchy stopped when overall survival in the whole enrolled population missed, so the survival figure clinicians quote for the assay-positive group was never formally tested.
questions.next: If the assay disagrees with itself between trials, and some of the population it excludes responds anyway, can responsiveness be manufactured rather than looked for?

questions.ask: Where the assay calls the tumour uninflamed, can another drug make it respond to checkpoint blockade?
questions.rationale: The infiltrate an assay measures on one biopsy at one moment is not a fixed property of the tumour. Cytotoxic drugs and radiation release antigen and change what sits in the microenvironment. PARP inhibition leaves cytosolic DNA that drives an interferon response. Each of those is a way of manufacturing the condition the assay was looking for.
questions.experiment: Induction was tested first. Patients were allocated between short courses of radiation, cyclophosphamide, cisplatin or doxorubicin, or no induction at all, before a common PD-1 backbone, with no control group. A separate single-arm study gave radiation with a checkpoint inhibitor and looked for response in the lesions that were not irradiated. Concurrent combination was tested by randomising carboplatin against carboplatin with PD-L1 blockade. The PARP route was tested three times. One trial gave a PARP inhibitor with PD-1 blockade in disease unselected for BRCA status. One gave a PARP inhibitor run-in followed by added PD-L1 blockade in germline carriers. One gave chemotherapy-free maintenance with a PARP inhibitor, with or without PD-L1 blockade, after platinum.
questions.finding: Each of these combinations produces disease control in a minority. In the trial that enrolled irrespective of BRCA status the responses concentrated in tumours carrying a BRCA mutation, while the maintenance trial singles out durable control in tumours without one. The randomised platinum comparison favoured adding PD-L1 blockade on both progression-free and overall survival. The benefit there did not follow PD-L1 status, which is the reverse of the selection the first-line trials were built on. Response after the common checkpoint backbone differed by which induction preceded it, highest in the anthracycline cohort and next in the platinum cohort.
questions.limitation: None of these designs isolates what the immune agent adds. The induction trial allocated patients between priming cohorts but never compared those cohorts statistically. Its cohorts are small and only its first stage is reported, so the ranking of priming strategies is a hypothesis rather than a result. The radiation study had no control arm either, so a shrinking unirradiated lesion cannot be credited to the abscopal effect it was built to look for. The randomised platinum trial is an exploratory phase II and its result is not the confirmatory evidence the approved chemotherapy-immunotherapy regimens rest on. Two of the three PARP combinations are single arms, so the contribution of either drug cannot be separated out. The third randomised its two arms but judged each against a historical control of continued platinum rather than against the other, so the longer progression-free survival in the combination arm is not evidence that the immune agent did anything, and its clinical benefit rate ran the other way. Eligibility drifts as well. One PARP cohort required only HER2-negative disease. The maintenance trial defined triple-negative at a receptor staining threshold rather than at no expression. Hormone receptor-positive tumours sit inside both.
questions.next: If the immune agent needs a cytotoxic partner to work at all, does it matter how that cytotoxic is delivered?

trials.acronym: Pembrolizumab plus radiotherapy in metastatic TNBC

questions.ask: Does an antibody-drug conjugate do better than the chemotherapy it replaces, and does it belong in the first line?
questions.rationale: TROP2 sits on the surface of most triple-negative tumours. A conjugate puts a topoisomerase inhibitor inside the cells that carry it, at a dose higher than free drug would allow. If chemotherapy earns its place in these regimens by killing cells, a conjugate should earn more of it.
questions.experiment: The conjugate was first randomised against the physician's choice of single-agent chemotherapy in patients who had already been through several lines. It was then moved to the first line in two randomised trials that split the population by whether checkpoint blockade was an option. Where PD-L1 was positive the conjugate was given with pembrolizumab against chemotherapy with pembrolizumab. Where it was not, the conjugate was given alone against chemotherapy. A second TROP2 conjugate was randomised against the investigator's choice of chemotherapy in the first line. A platform study gave that second conjugate with PD-L1 blockade in two single-arm first-line cohorts, one taking all comers and one restricted to PD-L1-high tumours.
questions.finding: The conjugate beat chemotherapy in every randomised comparison, in later lines and in the first line, with a checkpoint partner and without one. The second conjugate beat chemotherapy on both progression-free and overall survival in the first line. The single-arm cohorts of conjugate with PD-L1 blockade report the highest confirmed response rate of any first-line regimen recorded at this position.
questions.limitation: Those cohorts have no control arm. They cannot show what the immune agent adds to the conjugate, and they do not validate other pairings of a conjugate with immunotherapy. The two cohorts differ in selection rather than in treatment, so their response rates are not a comparison with each other, and the PD-L1-high cohort is early with immature duration of response. In the randomised first-line combination the control arm was chemotherapy with pembrolizumab rather than the conjugate alone, so the trial does not say whether the checkpoint inhibitor is still needed once the conjugate is in the regimen. Neither first-line trial of the conjugate that carries the later-line evidence has reported overall survival yet, so the move forward rests on progression-free survival for that agent while the competing conjugate already has a survival result to show.
questions.next: Once the backbone is a conjugate for nearly everybody, which patients are still defined by a biomarker rather than by a line of treatment?

questions.ask: When a tumour is picked out by its histology or by an uncommon alteration rather than by its receptors, is there enough evidence to act on?
questions.rationale: A small number of tumours filed as triple-negative carry something else that is actionable: a metaplastic histology, a high tumour mutational burden, an activating HER2 mutation without amplification, or a mutation in a repair gene other than BRCA1 and BRCA2. None is common enough to support a randomised trial in breast cancer alone. Each has therefore been studied as a cohort of a basket or as a single arm.
questions.experiment: Dual checkpoint blockade was given to a metaplastic cohort of a rare-tumour basket, and separately to patients selected on tumour mutational burden within HER2-negative disease. A HER2 kinase inhibitor with trastuzumab was given to a cohort with an activating HER2 mutation in disease that was HER2-negative by conventional testing. A PARP inhibitor was given alone to tumours wild-type for BRCA1 and BRCA2 carrying a mutation in another repair gene. All four are single arms reporting response rate.
questions.finding: Every cohort produced responses. The HER2-mutant cohort responded most often of the four and the repair-gene cohort next. In the metaplastic cohort the responses were few and still running at the time of the report, and every responder there developed adrenal insufficiency. In the repair-gene cohort the regressions were confined to a single gene. None of these is a rate a clinic can plan around, because each rests on a cohort small enough that one more responder would move it.
questions.limitation: None of these is a trial of triple-negative disease. A clinic has to match its patient to the entry criterion and not to the label on the cell. The metaplastic cohort was entered on histology alone, and its publication describes the majority of its tumours as triple-negative. The mutational burden cohort was entered on burden within HER2-negative disease, so hormone receptor-positive patients, most of the cohort, are inside it, and its comparison by receptor status was exploratory. The subgroup in it that carries the message about where to set the burden threshold is a handful of patients in a prespecified correlative analysis rather than a randomised comparison, so it establishes no cut-off. The HER2 mutation cohort likewise took both receptor groups, and its intervals are reported at a looser confidence level than the rest of the registry uses. Single arms of this size in selected populations establish that a response can happen, not how often it will.
